support_validation.exact_reproduction: 40 draws of x_distortion blur_motion:1 per support pair (fixed RNG seed); pairs 3 and 4 reproduced the degraded target PIXEL-EXACTLY (PSNR 168.13 dB, residual = 0 across all 2040x1536 / 2040x1356 pixels). Pairs 0/1/2 reached 56.54 / 48.32 / 66.12 dB on their best draw. All 5/5 pairs exceed 40 dB within 40 draws.
support_validation.interpretation: The target is produced by exactly this pipeline; the residual PSNR spread across draws is the unknown random angle (the x_distortion kernel is quantized into discrete integer-shift kernels, so a draw can hit the generator's kernel exactly). The angle is a stochastic nuisance parameter that is not encodable in the pipeline (function, severity) format and is regenerated per sample at training time, matching the generator's own behavior.

analysis.rationale: R1 changed the R0 isotropic gaussian:1 model to blur_motion:1 based on angle-invariant statistics. R2 closes the question with exact reproduction: a blur_motion:1 draw reproduces support pairs 3 and 4 pixel-for-pixel and all 5 pairs exceed 40 dB within 40 draws, while every deterministic blur family tops out at 30.7 dB and motion:2 never exceeds 34.9 dB. No residual structure survives an exact draw, and on angle-mismatch draws the leftover residual is structured kernel-angle error (lag-1 autocorr 0.48, no 8x8 grid), not a missing degradation. Therefore no further pipeline change can improve the match; the correct output is the R1 pipeline unchanged. R1 model support PSNR 35.05 dB already reflects this. The only irreducible uncertainty is the random angle, which is not parameterizable in params and should remain random during training.
